summary: Azerbaijan’s mixed land-use approach combines afforestation, reforestation, sustainable forest management, rotational grazing and land restoration. Its clearest forward commitment is approximately 30,000 hectares of forest-land expansion by 2026—300 km², or about 2.6% of the 11,564 km² mapped as forest in 2022—while the passage gives a projected total forest-coverage figure of 12.3%. It reports forestry and land use across 12.19% of national land and grasslands and pastures across 28%; the latter is not directly comparable with the 4.3% grassland-only map class. For conservation, it cites 2022 LULUCF net sequestration of 5.2 MtCO₂eq, including 3.6 MtCO₂ of forest-land removals across 1.04 million hectares, nearly 90% of mapped forest area. It also reports 2016 absorption of 7.2 million tons CO₂ equivalent, double the 1990 level. No separate sustainable-agriculture area is specified.
